content: In Bākharzī's report Jāmī rebukes Yazdī: having sought a master in order to associate with an accomplished man, he first travelled naked of possessions but then “gave yourself into the power of every amir and bureaucrat”, and in trying to expound the principles of Sufism supplied a weak defense unbecoming to the leading men of the age; 'this is not the way of a friend or an advocate'.
refers_to_primary: Bākharzī, Maqāmāt-i Jāmī, 106-7 (Jāmī's words as reported)
